intro: This awareness course covered what a urinary catheter is, why people have one, and how clean, careful support prevents infection and problems.
points: This is awareness only — you may only do delegated catheter care with task-specific training, assessed competence and delegation by a registered nurse.
Never insert or remove a catheter, and never flush, unblock or reinsert one — observe and report, do not fix.
Clean your hands before and after any catheter contact; gloves never replace hand hygiene, and keep the closed system sealed.
Always keep the drainage bag below bladder level and off the floor, empty via the outlet tap, never by disconnecting.
Recognise infection signs — fever, cloudy or smelly urine, new confusion — and treat suspected sepsis as a medical emergency.
Support fluids unless restricted, keep meatal hygiene to mild soap and water, and protect the person's dignity and privacy throughout.
